thought.text: I'll now perform a non-destructive end-to-end login test using the documented method: temporarily setting a known bcrypt hash on R1 user (id=1), logging in via HTTP, and restoring the original hash byte-identically.

reasoning_content:
User 1 (R1, ldap=0) and user 4 (R2, ldap=0) are available for the DB login path. The temporary password swap and restoration is the exact same method the installer used (and the installer claims they restored it byte-for-byte identical), so it's fine to do. Steps:

1. Record the original hash: `$2y$10$rZXtILwVu9pCmYxViazwg.4L3JR6A/mWMFSjSm33i9t2/.mxRmsc2`
2. Set a known hash for Test1234: `$2y$10$0pxbymtWUIMNmtOKoeppNuJ8vf6Mc.OK0EXZebeFOqgSkIBLCHiz2` (the one generated above)
3. Execute `curl -c jar -d 'user=4874e97068325d2ec1c29b052bfd3a7f&pass=Test1234&login-submit=1' http://127.0.0.1:32789/login` and expect a 302 redirect to the start page
4. GET / using the jar → 200, "Startseite" is displayed in the title
5. Restore the original hash, and verify it's byte-for-byte identical

After that, log out. Let's execute this.

action.command:
ORIG='$2y$10$rZXtILwVu9pCmYxViazwg.4L3JR6A/mWMFSjSm33i9t2/.mxRmsc2'
TEMP='$2y$10$0pxbymtWUIMNmtOKoeppNuJ8vf6Mc.OK0EXZebeFOqgSkIBLCHiz2'
# 1) set temp hash
docker exec ddev-tfm-fachplanung-db mysql -udb -pdb db -e "UPDATE user SET password='$TEMP' WHERE id=1;" 2>&1
echo "set temp hash, exit=$?"
# 2) login
curl -s -c /tmp/cookies.txt -o /dev/null -w 'LOGIN POST: HTTP %{http_code} -> %{redirect_url}\n' -d 'login-submit=1&user=4874e97068325d2ec1c29b052bfd3a7f&pass=Test1234' http://127.0.0.1:32789/login
# 3) authenticated GET /
curl -s -b /tmp/cookies.txt -o /tmp/home.html -w 'AUTH GET /: HTTP %{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:32789/
grep -oE '<title>[^<]*</title>' /tmp/home.html | head -2
# 4) restore original hash
docker exec ddev-tfm-fachplanung-db mysql -udb -pdb db -e "UPDATE user SET password='$ORIG' WHERE id=1;" 2>&1
echo "restore, exit=$?"
# 5) verify byte-identical
NOW=$(docker exec ddev-tfm-fachplanung-db mysql -udb -pdb db -N -e 'SELECT password FROM user WHERE id=1;' 2>/dev/null)
echo "now : $NOW"
echo "orig: $ORIG"
[ "$NOW" = "$ORIG" ] && echo 'HASH RESTORED BYTE-IDENTICAL' || echo 'HASH MISMATCH!'
